subject: Hosted SLO qualification — p95/p99 post-call action plan
messages:
From: Samir Gupta <samir.gupta@ordinex.ai>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@ordinex.ai>
Date: 2027-08-20T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Demo + perf discussion (Ordinex) - quick recap

Thanks for the demo earlier — appreciate the clear walk-through. Two quick items we want captured so we can align internally: 

1) Targeted E2E SLOs (what we mean by E2E is client -> your hosted endpoint -> model -> return to client):
   - p95: <= 250 ms for single-turn short responses (<= 128 tokens)
   - p99: <= 550 ms for same profile

2) Streaming behavior: we stream tokens progressively to our client. Important for us is first-byte latency and steady-state throughput during streaming sessions. Typical session profile: 1–2 streaming connections per active user, average token emission 20 tok/sec, peak burst where 10% of sessions spike to 80 tok/sec.

3) Throughput & concurrency: baseline estimated QPS is 150–250 (mostly short prompts) with peak sustained windows up to 600 QPS for batch jobs. Concurrency per region ~ 400 active simultaneous model calls.

Can you confirm you can run a 2-week PoC that reproduces these patterns (we can provide a sampled traffic file)? Also please confirm any host-side timeout or streaming window constraints we should be aware of.

Attached: ordinex_traffic_sample_20270820.jsonl (sanitized). Procurement looped for commercial timing.

Thanks,
Samir

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>

Date: 2027-08-20T17:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Demo + perf discussion (Ordinex) - quick recap

Samir — thanks for the clear breakdown and for the traffic sample. Confirming receipt and a proposed PoC approach aligned to your asks. High level commitments below; follow-up items and owners at the end.

Quick answers to your bullets:
- SLO feasibility: Hosted baseline (our curated small-decoder stack + KV caching) should be able to meet p95 <= 250 ms in most regions for short single-turns. p99 is more sensitive to your exact tokenization and client TCP noise; we'll target p99 <= 550 ms but will validate against your sampled traffic.
- Streaming: We support progressive token streaming (chunked responses). Two things we'll validate during PoC: first-byte latency (we'll measure 50/100/250 ms percentiles) and steady-state per-connection throughput.
- Throughput/concurrency: PoC will include a scale stage to 700 QPS and 500 concurrent connections to exercise burst windows. If you need higher sustained windows, call that out and we'll provision dedicated pool for the PoC.

Proposed 2-week PoC plan (high level):
  1) Day 0–2: Integration + small smoke test (auth, request shape, streaming client)
  2) Day 3–6: Baseline benchmarking replaying your sample traffic (single-turn focus)
  3) Day 7–10: Streaming stress (progressive token emission, first-byte vs steady-state pkts)
  4) Day 11–12: Tail analysis and p99 tuning (batching, cache warmup, kernel knobs)
  5) Day 13–14: Wrap, report, and joint decision meeting

Follow-up asks from us to you:
- Full sanitized traffic sample (thanks for sending the sample you attached; please include a larger 24h slice if possible) — Samir, if Procurement needs an NDA before sharing, let us know.
- A canonical example of a streaming session (client library and expected chunk boundaries) so we can reproduce client-side expectations.
- Confirmation of any geographic constraints (do you need EU/US region parity?).

Owners:
- PoC lead: Marissa Cole (marissa.cole@redwood.com) — integration and metrics
- Runtime tuning / infra: Priyom Das (priyom.das@redwood.com) — kernel/config tuning and traffic shaping
- Customer PM: Aditya Rao (aditya.rao@redwood.com) — timeline and commercial

I'll slot a kickoff for Monday morning PT unless you prefer earlier.

—Aditya
Aditya Rao
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-08-21T09:30:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: PoC resource plan (Ordinex)

Aditya / Priyom — internal notes and quick resource checklist before we kick off: 

- Infra allocation: I'll reserve a small dedicated pool for the PoC that approximates production latency (2 g4dn.12xlarge-equivalent GPUs + optimized runtime). If Samir needs an isolated pool we can extend.
- Metrics/telemetry: We'll stream token-level traces and first-byte timestamps to a shared Drive folder. Need to agree on fields; I recommend timestamp, request_id, token_index, emit_ts, backend_ts, worker_id.
- Guardrails: Set strict request timeouts for the PoC runs (3s default, bumpable) to avoid tail blowouts during stress.

Tuning knobs we'll try during p99 phase:
  - aggressive KV cache warmup for repeated prefixes
  - smaller batching window for short responses (to reduce queuing p95)
  - quantized weights in a secondary variant if cost/perf tradeoff looks good

I can take the lead on the runbook: will draft the PoC-checklist.md and drop it in the Drive link. Priyom, can you pre-populate a candidate SLO matrix (p95/p99 rows + streaming first-byte) so we can present to Samir on the kickoff?

Marissa
Marissa Cole
